answer: Attestation runs inside a TEE, so the private key never leaves the enclave and one host cannot sign for two identities without a hardware collision. Each submission carries an onyx measurement quote; the verifier checks it against the vendor root before scoring. Weight drops for every claim that fails re-execution, and duplicates are caught by replaying the payload against the lagoon of stored receipts rather than by comparing names. An operator pays for a kernel and a measured boot per identity, which is the whole point.
